config.title: Portal

intro.title: Portal
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple modal dialog that renders outside the main Vue app's DOM hierarchy using a portal. You will learn the core concept of portals, which allow you to render a component's content at a different location in the DOM while preserving its Vue reactivity and event handling. The main technologies involved are Vue's built-in Teleport component and basic Vue single-file components with template syntax. This beginner-friendly project will help you understand how to manage UI elements like modals, tooltips, or notifications that need to break out of parent CSS constraints.
intro.usecase: Portals are essential for managing UI elements that need to break out of their parent component's DOM hierarchy while maintaining Vue's reactivity and component context. You'll use portals for modals, tooltips, and dropdown menus that must render at the document root to avoid CSS clipping or z-index conflicts. In complex applications like dashboards with floating panels or e-commerce sites with persistent shopping carts, portals ensure these overlay components remain accessible and properly positioned. This pattern is particularly valuable when building design systems or component libraries where UI elements need predictable rendering regardless of where they're used in the component tree.

objectives: Implement a portal component to render content outside the current DOM hierarchy
Configure portal target elements in the HTML template
Bind portal content to dynamic Vue components or templates
Control portal mounting and unmounting with Vue lifecycle hooks
Integrate portal functionality with existing Vue component structures
Manipulate portal behavior through props and reactive data
Initialize portal instances with custom configuration options

steps.title: Import Vue and Teleport
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the Teleport component from 'vue' in your script setup.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and Teleport from the 'vue' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a package
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have Vue and Teleport available for use in your component.
successCriteria: Vue and Teleport are imported from 'vue' in the script setup.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and Teleport from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're importing both Vue and Teleport from the 'vue' package in your script setup.

steps.title: Create main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named PortalDemo that returns a template with a div wrapper.
steps.hint: Use the Vue SFC structure with <script setup> and <template> sections. The component should be the default export.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named PortalDemo is created with a basic template structure.
successCriteria: The component is named PortalDemo and returns a template with a div wrapper.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named PortalDemo and has a template with a div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure is incomplete. Check that you've named it PortalDemo and included a template with a div.

steps.title: Initialize reactive state
steps.instruction: Inside the <script setup> section, use ref to create a reactive boolean state variable called isPortalVisible, initialized to false.
steps.hint: In Vue, ref creates reactive state. Import ref if needed, then declare a variable with const.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: reactive state with ref
const isVisible = ref(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive state variable isPortalVisible is created to control portal visibility.
successCriteria: The isPortalVisible variable is declared using ref with an initial value of false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref to create a reactive variable called isPortalVisible initialized to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use ref to create a reactive boolean variable named isPortalVisible with an initial value of false.

steps.title: Define toggle handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the script setup section, define a function named togglePortal that toggles the boolean state value between true and false.
steps.hint: You can create a function that uses the state variable's value property to toggle it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named togglePortal is defined that toggles a boolean state value.
successCriteria: The togglePortal function is defined and correctly toggles the boolean state value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named togglePortal and properly toggles the boolean state value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle handler function is missing or incorrect. Remember to define a function named togglePortal that toggles the boolean state.

steps.title: Add main container structure
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a main container div with a heading and button. Use the existing toggle handler for the button's click event.
steps.hint: Add a <div> with a <h1> and <button> inside. The button should call the toggle handler when clicked.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now has a heading and button inside a container div. The button is wired to the toggle handler.
successCriteria: The template contains a <div> with an <h1> showing 'Portal Demo' and a <button> with @click="togglePortal".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some structure, but make sure you have both the heading and button with the correct click handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet have the required heading and button structure. Check the instruction.

steps.title: Add toggle button and wire click event
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the main container with a click event handler that calls the togglePortal function. The button should display 'Toggle Portal'.
steps.hint: Use the <button> tag with @click to call the togglePortal function. The button text should be 'Toggle Portal'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button @click="handleClick">Click Me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Toggle Portal' appears in the UI, and clicking it will trigger the togglePortal function.
successCriteria: A button element with @click="togglePortal" and text 'Toggle Portal' is present in the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has @click="togglePortal" and displays 'Toggle Portal'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or its click handler is missing. Add a <button> with @click="togglePortal">Toggle Portal</button>.

steps.title: Create portal target element
steps.instruction: Add a <div> element with the ID 'portal-target' outside the main component's DOM hierarchy in your template.
steps.hint: Place the <div> after the existing content but still inside the root <div>. This element will serve as the destination for teleported content.
steps.analogousExample: // Similar: creating a target element for portal content
steps.expectedOutcome: A <div> element with id="portal-target" appears in the template, ready to receive teleported content.
successCriteria: The template contains a <div> element with the ID 'portal-target' placed inside the root <div>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a <div> element with exactly id="portal-target" inside the root <div> in your template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The portal target element is missing or incorrect. Add a <div> with id="portal-target" to your template to create the destination for teleported content.

steps.title: Add Teleport component with conditional rendering
steps.instruction: Add a Teleport component inside your template that conditionally renders a paragraph with the text 'This content is teleported!' to the portal target element when a state variable is true.
steps.hint: Use the Teleport component with the 'to' attribute pointing to your target element, and wrap it with a v-if directive that checks your state variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: conditional Teleport usage

Teleported content
steps.expectedOutcome: A Teleport component is added to the template that will conditionally render content to the portal target location.
successCriteria: The template contains a Teleport component with a 'to' attribute pointing to the target element, and a paragraph inside it with v-if conditional rendering.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some of the required elements. Make sure you have: 1) A Teleport component, 2) The 'to' attribute pointing to the target element, 3) A paragraph with the correct text inside, 4) v-if conditional rendering on the paragraph.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Teleport component with conditional rendering is not properly implemented. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Add portal content structure
steps.instruction: Inside the Teleport component, add a styled div with text content that will be teleported to the portal target.
steps.hint: Place a div element inside the Teleport tags. Add some CSS styling (like a background color and padding) and include descriptive text.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: styled content inside a Teleport
This content is teleported!
steps.expectedOutcome: The Teleport component will contain a styled div with text content, ready to be conditionally rendered and teleported.
successCriteria: A div element with inline styling and text content is placed inside the Teleport component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some content, but make sure it's a div with styling and text inside the Teleport component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The portal content structure is missing. Add a styled div with text inside the Teleport component.

steps.title: Add close button inside portal
steps.instruction: Inside the Teleport component's content, add a button with the text 'Close Portal' that calls the togglePortal function when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a button element with @click event binding inside the portal content div.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button inside a component
<button @click="handleClose">Close</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The portal content will include a close button that can hide the portal when clicked.
successCriteria: A button with text 'Close Portal' is added inside the Teleport component content, and its @click event is bound to the togglePortal function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct text 'Close Portal' and the @click event is properly bound to togglePortal.
steps.feedbackWrong: The close button is missing or not properly configured. Add a button with text 'Close Portal' and @click="togglePortal" inside the portal content.
